outcome_intro: Ask your AI why a user is locked out of Duo and get the cause and the one fix that applies, then let it unlock them, issue a single-use bypass code, or move them to a new phone after you approve the plan. For an MSP it reads every customer subaccount at once: who can skip MFA, who never enrolled, and which customers are near their user limit.

instead_of_say.instead: Log in to the Duo Admin Panel, switch to the customer's account, search the user, then read their status, groups, phones, bypass codes and recent failed logins across four pages before deciding what to fix
instead_of_say.say: Jane at Acme is locked out of Duo. What's wrong and what's the fix?

instead_of_say.instead: Open every customer account one at a time before a security review, counting users in bypass, locked out, or never enrolled
instead_of_say.say: Which of our customers have users who can skip MFA right now?

instead_of_say.instead: Ask the caller which company they work for, then search one customer account after another until the username turns up
instead_of_say.say: Which customer is jdoe@example.com in, and are they locked out?

pain_points: A Duo lockout ticket is never one lookup. The answer is spread across the user's status, a group that can override it, their phones, any bypass codes already issued, and the last day of failed logins, and in the Admin Panel each of those is a different page.

An MSP runs every customer as a separate Duo subaccount with its own API host, so a question as simple as 'which customer is this caller in' or 'who across our book can skip MFA' means opening each account in turn.

Bypass codes outlive the emergency they were issued for. A code with no expiry or unlimited reuse is a standing hole in MFA, and nothing in the console lists them across a tenant with the admin who issued each one.

different_vs_wrappers: Duo's official client libraries ([duo_client_python](https://github.com/duosecurity/duo_client_python), [duo_api_golang](https://github.com/duosecurity/duo_api_golang)) sign requests and leave the workflow to you, and a thin MCP wrapper maps one tool to one endpoint. A lockout is never one endpoint, and an MSP's customers each sit behind their own API host. This skill signs every request itself, routes any command to a customer by name, and ships the composite answers: lockout triage reads the user, groups, phones, bypass codes and recent failures and returns the fix that applies; the fleet commands fan out across every subaccount in one call.
different_vs_vendor: The Duo Admin Panel shows one customer at a time and spreads a lockout diagnosis across several pages. This skill answers the help-desk and MSP questions from the AI you already use, across every subaccount at once, and its MFA fixes (lockout fix, phone-swap, enrollment chase) are previewed plans you approve before anything changes. It complements the Admin Panel: policies and application setup stay there.

faqs.a: Yes, on paid ChatGPT plans. ChatGPT connects to remote MCP servers over HTTPS: set CISCO_DUO_MCP_HTTP_TOKEN, run cisco-duo-mcp --transport http, and put its /mcp endpoint behind an HTTPS tunnel or your own reverse proxy. ChatGPT connectors sign in with OAuth or not at all and cannot send that bearer token, so ChatGPT also needs an OAuth-capable gateway in front of the endpoint that adds it. Step-by-step in the install guide.

faqs.q: Do I need to know how to code?
faqs.a: No. Paste one sentence into Claude Code or Codex and your agent does the install, or run a one-line installer. You enter your credentials once.

faqs.q: Is my Cisco Duo data safe?
faqs.a: Your data stays on your machine. The CLI, MCP server and the local mirror are all local, and the Duo secret key is used only to sign each request; it is never sent to Duo or anywhere else. The AI sees query results, not raw bulk data, and credentials are never bundled or transmitted by MSP Skills.

faqs.q: Do I need a Duo MSP (parent) account?
faqs.a: No. With an Admin API application in a single Duo account, every command except the fleet commands works against that account. As an MSP, create the Admin API application in your parent account with subaccount permissions (at least Grant accounts - Read): --account-id (or CISCO_DUO_ACCOUNT_ID) then runs any command against one customer, and fleet summary, fleet risk and fleet find-user cover every customer at once.

faqs.q: Which Duo Admin API permissions does it need?
faqs.a: Grant only what your workflow uses; the permission set is the strongest control you have. Read-only work (triage, audits, failures) needs Grant resource - Read, Grant read log and Grant read information. As an MSP, --account-id and the fleet commands also need Grant accounts - Read, because the CLI looks each customer up in your parent account's subaccount list, and the user-limit column of fleet summary needs Grant user limits - Read. Unlocking users, issuing bypass codes, swapping phones and re-sending enrollment emails add Grant resource - Write. Administrator commands need Grant administrators - Read or - Write, and billing set-user-limit needs Grant user limits - Write.

faqs.q: Is it safe to let an AI issue bypass codes?
faqs.a: Only with a human in the loop, and the commands are built for that. lockout fix, phone-swap and enrollment chase print a plan and change nothing until you add --apply. A bypass code from lockout fix is single-use, expires in an hour by default and keeps any existing codes. Verify the caller through a channel other than the ticket first (users send-verification-push sends them a Duo Push). Set CISCO_DUO_MCP_READ_ONLY=1 and the MCP server hides lockout fix, phone-swap and enrollment chase, and its API tool refuses every non-GET call.

faqs.q: Will this hit my Duo API rate limits?
faqs.a: Rarely. The client paces itself to Duo's rate-limit responses and backs off and retries when Duo answers 429. The fleet commands make a few calls per customer subaccount; fleet risk also pages users and bypass codes, caps that scan with --max-scan-pages, and flags any customer where the cap stopped it. Duo recommends polling authentication logs at most once a minute, so do not loop failures faster than that.

faqs.q: Will this replace the Duo Admin Panel?
faqs.a: No, it complements it. Policies, applications and directory sync stay in the Admin Panel. This skill answers the help-desk and MSP questions the panel makes you click through - lockout diagnosis, phone swaps, cross-customer risk and capacity - from your AI.
Free. Apache-2.0 licensed. You pay only for whichever AI agent you already use.

governance_summary: The skill reads Duo users, phones, groups, bypass codes, hardware tokens, admins, authentication logs and MSP subaccounts, and it can unlock users, issue bypass codes, attach and activate phones, send enrollment emails, delete users and factors, manage administrators, and create or delete customer subaccounts. Reads, sync and every preview are safe to allow. Anything that grants an authentication factor - an unlock, a bypass code, an activation link, a new phone - is human-in-the-loop only, after the caller's identity is verified. Deleting users or factors, administrator changes, billing changes and subaccount create or delete are operator-only. The strongest control is the Admin API application's permission set: an application without Grant resource - Write cannot unlock a user, issue a bypass code or touch a phone, and one without Grant administrators - Write or Grant accounts - Write cannot change administrators or customer accounts.

users send-verification-push, phones send-sms-installation, groups create, tokens resync, identity-verification start, identity-verification cancel
safety_tiers.policy: Preview with --dry-run (or the command's own preview), then a reviewed write

safety_tiers.policy: Human-in-the-loop only, after verifying the caller through a separate channel
